KR.read: Two distinct measures exist for Korea skincare and should not be summed: a HIGH-confidence domestic retail market size of KRW 7.653tn (~US$5.18bn equivalent, 2025, Euromonitor) and a HIGH-confidence export figure of US$8.54bn (EXPORT_FOB, 2025, ~75% of Korea's total cosmetics exports, MFDS). The export number is larger than the retail number because they measure different things (overseas sales vs. domestic sell-through), not because exports exceed the home market. Separate UN Comtrade HS 3304 data show Korea exported US$8.567bn to the world in 2024 (EXPORT_FOB) but only US$0.0656bn of that went to India [CORRIDOR]; HS 3304 also blends makeup with skincare, so this is not a skincare-only cut.
KR.trend: Domestic retail grew a modest 1.0% YoY in 2025 (Euromonitor, RETAIL), while skincare-led exports grew 11.6% YoY in 2025 (MFDS, EXPORT_FOB) - two different bases moving at different speeds. No cagr_forecast is present for either measure.
KR.caveats: The retail and export figures are both HIGH confidence but sit on different value_basis (RETAIL vs EXPORT_FOB) and must never be netted; the Comtrade HS 3304 figures additionally mix makeup into the skincare total.

IN.read: India's skincare market is sized at US$9.06bn (2025, RETAIL, LOW confidence, IMARC) - LOW because it is an aggregator estimate rather than a primary source. Two market-share reads of skincare's weight in adjacent baskets diverge structurally rather than contradicting each other: IMARC puts skincare/sun care at 35% of total BPC, while Grand View Research puts skincare at 49% of a narrower "cosmetics" basket - different denominators, not comparable directly. HIGH-confidence UN Comtrade data show India importing US$0.844bn of HS 3304 goods (skincare plus makeup) from the world in 2024, of which US$0.140bn came from Korea specifically [CORRIDOR] and US$0.188bn from China; a separate ESTIMATE (not a primary figure, methodology shown) derives import dependence at 9.3%, implying roughly 91% of the market by value is domestically supplied.
IN.trend: No growth_yoy or cagr_forecast DataPoint exists for the overall India skincare market, so growth direction cannot be assessed from current data at the segment level. IMARC's own notes on the market-size figure reference a forward-looking trajectory to US$18.38bn by 2034 (~7.49% CAGR), but this is a forecast from a LOW-confidence source, not an observed trend. A single-company data point (Minimalist, NET_REALISATION, MEDIUM confidence, FY24) shows revenue up from Rs184cr (FY23) to Rs347cr - one D2C brand's growth, not the market.
IN.caveats: Most India skincare figures here are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates (IMARC, Grand View Research, MarkNtel, IMA Pro) rather than primary-sourced, and none states organised-vs-unorganised coverage explicitly; several retail-price points are individual K-beauty SKUs [CORRIDOR], not market-wide figures.

combined.read: A like-for-like size comparison is possible here because both sides carry a value_usd_bn figure on a RETAIL basis: Korea's domestic retail market converts to ~US$5.18bn (2025, HIGH confidence) versus India's ~US$9.06bn (2025, LOW confidence) - India reads larger on this comparison, though the confidence gap (HIGH vs LOW) means it should be treated as indicative, not precise. Korea's US$8.54bn EXPORT_FOB export figure sits on a different value_basis and cannot be netted against India's retail figure. The Korea-to-India corridor is real but small and inconsistent between reporting sides: Korea reports US$0.0656bn of HS 3304 (skincare plus makeup) exports to India in 2024 [CORRIDOR], while India reports US$0.140bn of HS 3304 imports from Korea in the same year [CORRIDOR] - a mismatch consistent with FOB-vs-CIF differences and mirror-trade-statistics discrepancies, and neither figure isolates skincare from makeup. A substantial set of individual K-beauty SKU retail prices captured from Nykaa and Blinkit (COSRX, Laneige, Innisfree, Anua, Beauty of Joseon, and others) document this corridor at the shelf level, but these are product-level price points, not a market-size figure for the corridor itself.
